submitted.rationale: Index 9 (V0.858 Zr0.142) had the highest measured photocurrent, 7.58e-6 A. That is about 2x index 0 (V 0.88, 3.73e-6 A) and 33x index 13 (near ZrV2O7, 2.3e-7 A). The phases are ZrV2O7 (predicted gap 2.7–3.1 eV) and V2O5 (lower gap), both on the MACE hull. V-rich mixtures of the two absorb the 3.22 eV light and perform best. The peak appears to be around V ≈ 0.85.

rejected.reason: Measured 2.3e-7 A. Near-phase-pure ZrV2O7 has a gap too close to the photon energy and performs poorly.
Zr-rich compositions are dominated by wide-gap ZrO2, which should not absorb 3.22 eV light. Not measured.

consultations.verdict: Support: ZrV2O7 is on the MACE hull and has predicted HSE gap 3.14 eV, just below the 3.22 eV photons, so it should absorb. Index 13 (V 0.673) sits closest to ZrV2O7 stoichiometry.

Support: V2O5 is on the MACE hull and has a lower gap than ZrV2O7, so it absorbs 3.22 eV light more strongly. The V-rich end (index 0, V 0.88) should be a V2O5+ZrV2O7 mixture, which could form a heterojunction and give more photocurrent than index 13.

Mostly uninformative, weak support. The PBE gap for ZrV2O7 is 2.75 eV, so V-rich mixtures of ZrV2O7 and V2O5 all absorb. Measurements show photocurrent rising sharply toward V-rich compositions. Index 9 (V 0.858) tests just below the best measured point.
